key_impacts: PHIVOLCS issued tsunami alert level 3 (immediate evacuation) at 21:01 local time covering coastal areas of several provinces.
No significant tsunami was observed and no damages were reported; PHIVOLCS cancelled the alert at 00:10 on 1 September 2012.
Strong shaking was felt in Pacific coastal areas of the central-southern Philippines with reported intensities IV–VI or V–VII.
Evacuations took place in most surveyed barangays; an estimated average of 80% of residents evacuated, while one barangay did not.

Communication problems (delays, power cuts, mobile outages, and a wrong radio broadcast) led to delayed/distorted messages; in Guiuan the modeled wave travel time (~10 min) was shorter than the warning release (14 min after the quake).
missing_information: Exact tsunami wave heights by location were not reported.
Comprehensive counts of evacuees and non-evacuees are unavailable.
Detailed locality-by-locality arrival times of any unusual waves were not provided.
Specific municipality with the incorrect radio broadcast was not identified.
Full damage assessment details are not provided (report notes no damages observed).

key_impacts: A tsunami alert was raised in the Philippines following the 27 February 2010 Chile earthquake.
The source was distant, so time was not a critical factor for the related survey.
Only a very small wave was noted in the Philippines and no damages were reported.
missing_information: Specific Philippine coastal areas included in the alert are not stated.
Alert level issued by PHIVOLCS is not specified.
Timing of the alert issuance and wave arrival in the Philippines is not provided.

Wave heights in the Philippines are not detailed.
